evals.prompt: Je veux planifier la campagne de mon single qui sort dans environ un mois. Je suis surtout sur Instagram et TikTok.
evals.expected_output: A conversational one-question-at-a-time interview in French that skips anything the profile or presskit already answers, follows the single-specific flow (story, pre-save), and closes with the mandatory anything-else question before emitting the readiness sentinel.
assertions: Asks one question per turn in plain text, with no markdown or emojis
Does not re-ask the platforms or the target date, both stated in the prompt
Does not re-ask the city, genre, language, or career stage, all present in the profile
Every reply is in French and no reply mixes languages
No turn runs longer than three sentences
The final question asks about time constraints, unavailability, label requirements, and deadlines
Frames the budget question so that $0 is an acceptable answer
Ends with the summary followed by a single [READY_TO_GENERATE]

evals.prompt: Parfait, génère le plan. Le budget est de 150 $.
evals.expected_output: A phased plan of roughly 14-20 tasks from 3-4 weeks before to 1-2 weeks after, every asset paired create-then-post, only Instagram and TikTok used, task costs reconciled against $150, posting times in the artist's local timezone.
assertions: Every create task precedes its post task by 1-3 days
No platform outside Instagram and TikTok appears in any task
Estimated task costs sum to $150 or less
total_estimated_cost equals the sum of the task estimated_costs
Runs reconcile-budget.ts rather than summing task costs in prose
No paid line sits below its product's stated minimum — Spotify Ads Manager appears only at $250 or more, a publicist only at $1000 or more
Each task carries type, platform group, content brief, day offset, cost, and posting time
Posting times are given in the artist's local time and no time is labelled EST, PST, MST, CST, or AST

evals.prompt: En fait je n'ai aucun budget. Refais le plan à 0 $.
evals.expected_output: The same phased plan with no paid tactic in it — every task organic, every paid task rewritten into its organic equivalent or dropped rather than left standing at a cost of zero.
assertions: Every task's estimated cost is 0 and total_estimated_cost is 0
No task title or content brief names a paid product such as Spotify Ads Manager, Spotify Marquee, Spark Ads, a paid playlist service, or a publicist
Each dropped paid tactic is either replaced by a named organic equivalent or explicitly removed
The task count stays within the 14-20 range rather than collapsing when the paid tasks go

evals.prompt: Fais-moi le plan, je te dirai pour l'argent plus tard.
evals.expected_output: A plan whose total is the real sum of its task costs, with no invented ceiling and an explicit note that no budget was captured.
assertions: Says plainly that no budget was captured
Does not state or imply a budget ceiling the artist never gave
total_estimated_cost equals the sum of the task estimated_costs
Does not zero the task costs

evals.prompt: En fait regénère tout, je veux un angle différent.
evals.expected_output: A warning that regeneration reassigns what each sort_order means rather than deleting anything, naming the tasks whose meaning shifts and the hand-edited caption now attached to different work, then a wait for confirmation.
assertions: States that task statuses, captions, content links, and calendar ids survive the regeneration
Does not claim the existing tasks, their progress, or their captions will be deleted
Names which tasks change meaning because sort_order is reassigned
Says that a shorter plan leaves trailing tasks needing manual deletion
Produces no new plan until the artist confirms

evals.prompt: Écris les captions pour la publication du jour de sortie.
evals.expected_output: One caption per selected platform in that platform's native style, grounded in the artist's real assets, with hooks written as actual first lines and specific CTAs.
assertions: One caption for Instagram and one for TikTok, each in that platform's conventions
Instagram caption carries 8-12 hashtags and a CTA
TikTok caption is hook-first
CTAs are specific, never generic phrasing like check it out
Any metric cited matches the 4,200 monthly listeners on record
No press quote or award appears, because the presskit holds none

evals.prompt: Ça vaut-tu la peine de mettre de l'argent sur Spotify Ad Studio pour un single?
evals.expected_output: A plain answer that Spotify Ad Studio has a $250 minimum and so is not available at this budget, what to do with $150 instead, and the knowledge page the floor comes from — with no campaign, task or memory written.
assertions: Answers in French, matching the prompt
Says Spotify Ad Studio needs at least $250 and names the campaign's $150 as the reason it is out
Names paid-promotion.md, or another knowledge page, as where the floor comes from
Says the pricing is a heuristic to confirm before spending, not a quoted price
Nothing is written — no campaign, no task, no memory
Points at digital-marketing-plan if the artist wants the spend actually reallocated

evals.prompt: Combien de temps avant la sortie je devrais commencer à poster?
evals.expected_output: The pre-release window from the playbook — roughly three to four weeks of build-up before the date, with the editorial pitch deadline named — attributed to the knowledge page, and no plan generated.
assertions: Answers in French, matching the profile locale
Gives the 3-4 week pre-release window from marketing-fundamentals.md
Names the page the window comes from
Does not generate a plan or a task list
Hands off to digital-marketing-plan for the actual dated plan

given.conversation: Earlier in the interview the strategist said the budget was $0, carried from the project. The artist replied: 'how do you know its 0$? I can put 50$ on the campaign.' The strategist answered 'Fixing that now: budget is $50.' Asked what the campaign is for, the artist said 'I want more streams, and more following.'

evals.expected_output: A campaign row carrying budget 50 — the corrected figure, not the project's 0 — and primary_goal as an ordered array holding both streams and followers, streams first. total_estimated_cost comes from reconcile-budget.ts, never a sum done in prose.
assertions: budget is saved as 50, not 0 — the correction wins over the value carried from the project
primary_goal holds BOTH streams and followers, ordered, not one of them
total_estimated_cost is set from reconcile-budget.ts rather than left null or added up in prose
Nothing the artist did not say is written — no inferred budget, no assumed goal
The row is checked against the conversation field by field before the write

given.artist.marketing_tasks: 20 tasks written, every estimated_cost 0, total_estimated_cost null

evals.prompt: Is the budget right on that plan?
evals.expected_output: Calls the reconcile_budget tool with the campaign id and reports what it returned — the sum before, the sum after, and the total it set. Never adds the costs up in prose, and never tells the artist to run a bash script.
assertions: Calls the reconcile_budget tool rather than summing the costs itself
Does not instruct the artist to run reconcile-budget.ts from a shell — there is no shell here
Reports the total it set, and says plainly if any task cost was scaled down
Leaves total_estimated_cost set rather than null

evals.prompt: I want more streams I guess. I don't really know what a good number is.
evals.expected_output: Suggests a documented, reachable target rather than inventing a stream count — 200 pre-saves, where the 40-60% first-week algorithmic lift appears, or a save rate above 20%, which Spotify weights ~3x above stream volume. Records it with its date as success_target and names the tasks that move it.
assertions: Does not invent a stream-count target — a stream count is an outcome nobody controls
Offers 200 pre-saves or a >20% save rate, and says why each is the number that matters
Gets a date attached, so the goal is time-bound and checkable
Saves it to success_target in the artist's own words
Names which tasks in the plan move that specific number

evals.prompt: With $50, is there anything worth doing with ads?
evals.expected_output: Opens paid-promotion.md, reports that Meta publishes no dollar minimum and $5-10/day is a working budget, so $50 buys roughly 10 days of Instagram/Facebook traffic ads. Says TikTok (above $50/day) and Spotify (CA$250) are out at this budget, and cites the floors rather than recalling them.
assertions: Says YES — Meta has no published minimum and $50 runs there
Does NOT claim $50 clears no ad floor; that is true of TikTok and Spotify only
Names the floors it rules out and where each number comes from
Proposes a concrete objective — Traffic to the pre-save or smart link, never Brand Awareness
Opens the knowledge page rather than answering from memory

evals.expected_output: Writes the ideas to marketing_ideas before saying a menu exists, shows the menu, and after any task is written the campaign's total_estimated_cost equals the sum of task costs — never null.
assertions: Content ideas are WRITTEN to marketing_ideas, not described in prose
The menu the artist sees is the rendered numbered list, not an announcement that one exists
No second campaign row is created for a title that already exists
total_estimated_cost is set and equals the sum of task costs — never left null
No task cost exceeds what the stated budget allows once reconciled

evals.expected_output: The album plan contains a tracklist reveal as a dated task in the T-30 to T-14 window, in one of the shapes on marketing-fundamentals.md, naming any features it announces.
assertions: The plan contains a tracklist reveal task — a record's tracklist is content, not an afterthought
Its date falls between 30 and 14 days before the target date, after the announcement and before launch week
It commits to ONE shape — all at once, progressive, feature reveal, or guess the list — not four tasks
The task title says what the thing is, not 'tracklist content'
It is one task for the release, never one per track

evals.expected_output: A single's plan contains no tracklist reveal — a single has no tracklist — and the slot goes to lyric-led and hook content instead.
assertions: No tracklist reveal task appears anywhere in the plan
If the artist asks for one, the reply says a single has no tracklist and offers a lyric reveal or a credit reveal instead

evals.expected_output: An album plan shaped as the six movements of the record arc, not a single's four-week arc with a longer date range — including a release week that spotlights a different track each day.
assertions: Release week contains more than one post — a different track spotlighted on separate days, not a single release-day announcement
At least one post-release task is a mini-campaign for an individual track, not a generic 'keep posting' task
The pre-release window runs longer than the four weeks a single gets
The plan does not treat the record as one undifferentiated object — individual track titles appear in task titles

evals.prompt: Je veux planifier la campagne de mon EP.
evals.expected_output: The record's intake asks about the pre-save — it is no longer single-only — and the question reads as the release's own link, distinct from the lead single's.
assertions: The pre-save question IS asked for an EP, phrased as the pre-save for the release itself
The plan contains a pre-save task for the EP as a whole, not only for the lead single
Every reply is in French
The rollout-order question is still asked, and the pre-save question does not replace it

artist.presskit.long_bio: Odile Ray est une autrice-compositrice-interprète folk basée à Montréal.

evals.expected_output: Asks the five website questions one at a time (first language, domain, store, newsletter, Bandsintown), each skippable; then runs `bun run website:build`, reports the file it wrote and the missing list with the command that fills each gap — pre-save for the EP, the English bio, past shows — and asks for the first gap rather than inventing content. Deploys only after the artist has seen the preview and said yes.
assertions: Asks one question per turn and accepts 'none' or a blank for every one of the five
Runs `bun run website:build` rather than writing HTML in the conversation
Reports the missing list from the build output, naming the pre-save link and the English bio as gaps
Does not invent a bio, a quote, a show or a merch item to fill a gap
Does not run `website:deploy` before the artist has seen the preview and agreed
Never asks for the bio, the socials or the releases — all three are on file

evals.prompt: Mets mon site en ligne maintenant.
evals.expected_output: Refuses cleanly, in French: with no releases, no bio and no photos on file the page would be a name on a black background, and says which department fills each — the presskit intake for bio and photos, the catalog for releases — before offering to build a preview anyway so the artist sees the gaps.
assertions: Every reply is in French
Does not deploy
Names the presskit intake as what fills the bio and photos, and the catalog as what fills the releases
Offers the preview build as the next step, not a deploy
